HEAD: BEHOLDA, THE BENEVOLENT BEHOLDER -- sheet 2, her moves for a tactics game. ### The goblin, redone (added 10-07, on Griz's word)

Griz, 10-07: *"Redoing goblins while we have an expanded art department, please the copypasta for all the 16 bit sprite animation rows we'll need for them"*. The goblin is the Game Show's first wave (its lane §3 D: *"the most famous monsters that fit the CR requirements (i.e. goblins)"*) and a Quaternius Blob Orc till now (`goblin_p1`: idle, walk, attack). Its kit (`deep16/data/foes.js` goblin, SRD 5.1): Scimitar, Shortbow (loosed when nothing is in reach), Nimble Escape as Disengage and a step back (`deep16/js/traits.js`); the SRD's other half of Nimble Escape, Hide as a bonus action, is not built for it. The look follows the 8-bit's goblin (`js/bestiary-art.js` A.goblin: green skin, yellow eyes, the ears swept wide, brown leather, a scimitar), with the SRD's AC 15 drawn as leather and a shield.

**Came back 10-07, IN HAND** (Griz: *"Should be GPT Goblins in _src"*; `deep16/_src/Goblin-GPT1..4.png`, all four, every row asked for): `goblin_p2` by `tools/goblin-sheet.py` over `tools/sheetrows.py` -- each sheet scaled by the figure's area against sheet 1's turnaround (about 36 hunched from the side, 41 from the front), sheets 2-4 toned to sheet 1's olive (GPT drew them a yellower green), the back idle's five frames played 1 2 3 4 5 4; Nimble Escape's hop plays before its steps (`deep16/js/traits.js`), the arrow leaves on the shortbow's release frame (the row's `release`, `deep16/js/battle.js`), Hide is cut but nothing plays it; the wagon's glamour goblins wear it too. `goblin_p1` stays on disk till your look. The pastes below are kept for a re-roll.

**Four sheets. Sheet 1 first; sheets 2-4 attach what sheet 1 brought back.** Sheet 1 is the side rows with the portrait and turnaround; sheet 2 its tricks, side-on; sheet 3 from the front (facing S), sheet 4 from behind (facing N). The seat's calls, the Goose/Rascal precedent: Fall and Prone side-on only (a body on the floor reads from any side), Hide side-on only, Climb side and behind (a wall is climbed facing it). Every row has one frame count in every facing (Idle 6, Walk 8, Scimitar 6, Shortbow 6, Nimble Escape 4, Flinch 4, Climb 6). No arrow in flight anywhere (the grid draws its own, `FX.projectile`; a loose arrow would be cut onto the nearest frame).

**When they come back:** `deep16/_src/goblin_<gpt|grok>_1..4.png`, a cutter `tools/goblin-sheet.py` over `tools/sheetrows.py` to `goblin_p2` (then `foes.js` goblin `sheet`). Rows: turnaround -> idle by facing where a facing has no row; Idle -> idle; Walk -> walk; Scimitar -> `scimitar` (battle.js plays a row named for the attack) and `attack` (the fallback); Shortbow -> `shortbow`; Nimble Escape -> `nimble` (new: `tools/pixelate.py` ANIM_ORDER and FPS, `deep16/js/ui.js`'s play-once rule, the "darts back" in `deep16/js/traits.js` plays it before the walk); Hide -> `hide` (new; nothing plays it until the goblin's Hide is built); Climb -> climb; Flinch -> flinch; Fall -> hurt; Prone -> prone (`S.proneRow`). Sheet 3's rows for facing S, sheet 4's for N, the diagonals the side rows. Then `deep16/?show=goblin` and a fresh eyes row.

GOBLIN, SHEET 1 (the look, side-on; no reference to attach):

HEAD: THE GOBLIN -- sheet 1, a foe for a tactics game. A goblin: a small, scrawny, wiry humanoid, hunched, about half a man's height, with green skin, a flat face with a broad flat nose, a wide mouth of small sharp teeth, small yellow eyes, and long pointed ears sweeping out and up from the sides of its head. A scruffy brown leather jerkin with a dark belt, dark brown leggings, bare clawed feet. A curved steel scimitar in its right hand, a small round wooden shield strapped to its left forearm, a shortbow and a quiver of arrows slung across its back. Sly and quick, never quite still. Rows: Idle (6: crouched on bent knees, shifting its weight, its head darting left and right and its ears twitching, the scimitar held low and ready); Walk (8: a quick hunched scurry, the scimitar low, the shield up); Scimitar (6: a quick vicious slash at a foe in front of it, then back on guard); Shortbow (6: the scimitar hung at its belt, it pulls an arrow from the quiver on its back, nocks it, draws the shortbow with the bow in its shield hand and looses; draw no arrow in flight -- the last frame holds the empty bow); Flinch (4: struck, it jolts back with its eyes squeezed shut and its ears flattened, then recovers); Fall (6: knocked out, it topples backward and lies flat on its back, the scimitar dropped beside it; the last frame lies on the ground); Prone (2: knocked flat but alive and struggling: lying on the ground, then pushing itself up).

### The hobgoblin and the hobgoblin sergeant (added 10-07, on Griz's word)

Griz, 10-07: *"copy pasta for 3 and 4 please"* (3: the next goblinoids, the bestiary lane §6.4; 4: the Game Show's art asks, below). Both are Game Show wave foes and still Quaternius stand-ins (`hobgoblin_p1` the Orc, `hobsergeant_p1` the Orc Skull). Their kits (`deep16/data/foes.js`): the **hobgoblin** (SRD 5.1, CR 1/2, AC 18: chain mail and a shield) has a Longsword, a Longbow it looses when nothing is in reach, and Martial Advantage (+2d6 once a turn while an ally stands by the target, `deep16/js/battle.js`). The **sergeant** (game-original from the SRD's Hobgoblin and Veteran, CR 3, AC 18) swings the Longsword twice a turn and has Martial Advantage, but no bow. The look follows the 8-bit's (`js/bestiary-art.js` A.hobgoblin: orange skin, dark hair, a dark red tunic, a grey helm, a sword, a brown shield, a gold belt; the sergeant is the same figure tinted darker red).

**Four sheets each, one sheet an image** (the bugbear's finding: a file of every sheet came back as one packed image with soft frames). Sheet 1 first; sheets 2-4 attach what sheet 1 brought back. Same calls as the goblin: Fall and Prone side-on only, Climb side and behind, one frame count for each row in every facing, no arrow in flight.

**IN HAND (10-07, his: *"Hobgoblin and hobsergeant sheets are in _src"*):** `deep16/_src/Hobgoblin1..4.png` and `HobSergeant1..4.png`, cut by `tools/hobgoblin-sheet.py` to `hobgoblin_p2` and `hobsergeant_p2`, worn by both foes; `deep16/?show=hobgoblin,hobsergeant`. **As asked:** `deep16/_src/`, cut by a `tools/hobgoblin-sheet.py` over `tools/sheetrows.py` to `hobgoblin_p2` and `hobsergeant_p2` (then `foes.js` `sheet`). Rows: Idle -> idle; Walk -> walk; Longsword -> `longsword` and `attack`; **Longsword 2 -> `longsword2`** (battle.js plays an attack's second use in a turn on its numbered row, as claw2 does; it goes in pixelate's ANIM_ORDER); Longbow -> `longbow` (with a `release` frame, as the goblin's shortbow has); **Martial Advantage -> `martial`** (new: the drilled lunge, played on a melee blow when an ally stands by the target and the turn's Martial Advantage is unspent; on a miss too, since the drill is visible either way; the seat's call); Flinch -> flinch; Fall -> hurt; Prone -> prone; Climb -> climb. Sheet 3 plays facing S, sheet 4 facing N, the diagonals use the side rows. Then `deep16/?show=hobgoblin` and `?show=hobsergeant` and a fresh eyes row.

HEAD: THE HOBGOBLIN -- sheet 1, a foe for a tactics game. A hobgoblin: a goblinoid soldier, as tall as a man, upright and disciplined, broad in the shoulder. A plain steel helm with a nose guard; a coat of chain mail over a dark red tunic; a belt with a gold buckle; dark trousers and boots. A longsword in its right hand; a rectangular wooden shield banded in iron on its left arm; a longbow and a quiver of arrows slung across its back. A drilled soldier: it holds the line and never wastes a move. Rows: Idle (6: standing on guard behind its shield, the longsword held level, breathing slowly, its eyes moving across the field); Walk (8: a steady marching step, the shield up and the sword held ready); Longsword (6: a disciplined cut at a foe in front of it, stepping in behind the shield, then back on guard); Longbow (6: the longsword sheathed at its hip, it pulls an arrow from the quiver on its back, nocks it, draws the longbow with the bow in its shield hand and looses; draw no arrow in flight -- the last frame holds the empty bow); Flinch (4: struck, it rocks back behind its shield with its teeth gritted, then steadies); Fall (6: knocked out from STANDING: frame 1 on its feet and reeling, frame 2 tipping backward, frame 3 falling, frames 4 to 6 hitting the ground and lying flat on its back, the longsword dropped beside it); Prone (2: knocked flat but alive: lying on its side on the ground, then pushing itself up on one arm).

### The Game Show's props: the chest and the bed (added 10-07, on Griz's word)

The Game Show lane §3 F. **The chest** is where the audience's supplies land (seat 1's words for Ingrith: *"The chest by the lamp -- whatever the folk up top send down for you lands in it."*; the epic amulet's pop-up says "check the chest!"). Nothing draws it today. **The bed** is where the rests are taken between waves. Third Lamp's cots are the 8-bit's `y` tiles, which the grid draws as `deep16/js/iso.js` BLOCK `y`, a timber crib with slats and a bar, so they read as cradles, not beds. Both are props on one floor diamond each, drawn from a sheet as `deep16/js/circles.js` draws the wheel. The bed's glow when its rest is due is the code's job, not the art's.

**IN HAND (10-07):** his two sheets (`deep16/_src/Pixel Art Treasure Chest Animation Sheet.png`, `Pixel Art Cot Comparison A and B.png`) cut by `tools/gsprops-sheet.py` to `gschest_p1` (rows `shut`, `thump`, `open`, `opened`) and `gsbed_p1` (`a`, `b`: the two diagonals); the chest stands at Third Lamp's tower (`lampcircle` `chest`), the cots are drawn from the sheet instead of the crib (`cots`), `deep16/js/circles.js`. Seen in the pane: *"looks great from here in the pane"* · *"cots too"*.

HEAD: PROPS, THE SUPPLY CHEST -- a dwarven supply chest at a lamp station deep underground, where gifts from the surface arrive by magic. One sturdy chest, wider than it is deep: dark oak planks bound with iron bands, riveted iron corners, a heavy domed lid, a big iron lock plate on its front, and a small brass lamp emblem set in the middle of the lid. Its front faces the lower left. Rows: Shut (1: closed and still); Thump (3: something lands inside it from above: the chest jolts, the lid jumps open a crack with a flash of gold light, then slams shut with a puff of dust); Open (4: the lid swings up from shut to wide open, warm gold light spilling out from inside); Opened (2: the lid wide open, the inside glowing warm gold with a few small sparkles, the two frames flickering).

#### COMMON TAIL (pictures -- paste after each picture's head)

Behind the whole scene, huge and blurred, a single yellow eye.

#### P5. The chimney of wings

HEAD: THE CHIMNEY -- a narrow natural rock chimney seen from below, rising into darkness, filled with a spiral of thousands of bats streaming upward; a thin shaft of grey light far above.

### The clackers (the landlord's picture made flesh; asked 10-01; the sheet IN HAND 10-01)

Griz, 10-01: *"we're going to need an art-prompt description of the clackers it has envisioned to hope for something close when we eventually model it, try make one of those in blender so we have it later"*, and the same night, *"I had a problem with the 'later' on the clacker and there's a 16 bit animation sheet available for review"*: he ran Q2, and the sheet is on the grid (IN HAND above; `?npc=clacker` fields it, a block of our own in `deep16/data/foes.js` and `invented.json#clacker`, clacking its hooks at the start of each turn). The look below is read off the landlord's picture (`dev/visions/the-clackers.jpg`, the fourth it sends when fed) and the wiki's clacker cavern (`TarlynsPit/wiki/the-warrens.md`: a hook horror colony crowning the crook; the clacking is their language). The game never names them. Q1 (the model sheet) is still welcome for the Blender model below.

**The look, in words (for any prompt, any tool):** a hook horror. Tall and hunched, about nine feet if it ever straightened, its back bowed so the head hangs forward below the line of the shoulders. A small vulture's head on a thick neck: a long down-curved beak, pale bone, hooked at the tip; two small round yellow eyes set close above the beak's root; no ears, no crest. The whole body sheathed in small overlapping plates like cobblestones or old scales, dark green-grey, lighter on the ridges and black in the seams; a heavy chest and shoulders, a narrow waist. No hands: each long forearm ends in one huge curved hook of pale ivory bone, longer than the forearm, smooth and worn bright on its inner edge. At rest the hooks are carried raised and folded back, so they rise above the shoulders and curl forward over the head like a pair of scythes. Long bent legs, clawed feet, a stalking gait. The only colours are the grey-green hide, the bone of the beak and hooks, and the yellow of the eyes. It talks by striking its hooks together: clack, clack.

#### Q1. The clacker, a model sheet (for modelling it in 3D)

Paste alone (not with the COMMON TAIL above):

HEAD: CHARACTER MODEL SHEET FOR 3D MODELLING -- a hook horror: [paste the look, in words, above]. Orthographic views of the whole creature side by side, the same scale and the same baseline in each: FRONT, SIDE (facing right), BACK, and THREE-QUARTER FRONT; in each view it stands in its neutral hunch with the hooks raised over the shoulders. Beneath: a close-up of the head in profile and from the front (the beak, the eyes, how the plates run over the skull), a close-up of one forearm and its hook from the side (where bone meets plate), and a small figure of a human man beside the side view for scale. Flat even studio lighting, no cast shadows, no perspective, a plain light-grey background, clean lines. Concept art, not a painting: every form readable. No text but the view labels.

#### Q2. The clacker, a sprite sheet (for the grid, the day it fights)

HEAD: THE CLACKER -- a hook horror out of the deep caves: [paste the look, in words, above]. Large: twice a man's height hunched. Rows: Idle (8, the head bobbing, the hooks flexing), Walk (8, the hunched stride, hooks held high), Hook (8, one hook swung down and across), Clack (6, both hooks raised and struck together over the head: their speech and their war-cry), Climb (6, hooking up a rock wall), Hurt (6), Death (8).

**The model (10-01, a first pass):** `tools/clacker-blend.py` builds it from nothing in Blender 5.2 (`"C:/Program Files/Blender Foundation/Blender 5.2/blender.exe" -b --python tools/clacker-blend.py [-- previews]` writes `deep16/_src/clacker/clacker.blend`, gitignored, so the script is what the repo keeps). A Skin-modifier body with a plated-hide shader, swept bone hooks, beak and toe claws, yellow eyes; 23 bones; IDLE, WALK and ATTACK (the hooks raised in a V, crossed in an X at frame 17: the clack). It is in `tools/deep16-figures.json` as `clacker` (1.35 squares, about 86 px tall, the ettin's height) and runs through `tools/render-sprites.py`; nothing in the game uses it yet. Previews: `dev/visions/clacker-model-*.png`. **Short of the painting:** the body is a round blob, the legs frog-like, the head long rather than a domed vulture's skull, the hooks rod-straight from the front; a Q1 model sheet is what would true it.

Spell looks are NOT on this list: the pass draws them in code (and Blender can render a floating weapon), so the generator's days go to creatures.

16-bit pixel art animation sheet, SNES-era, crisp dark outline, readable at small size. Flat dark navy background. ONE sheet only, filling the whole image: no portrait, no turnaround, no title. Two rows, labelled Hurt Front and Hurt Back at the left, 8 frames each, numbered under each frame. Every frame stands apart with clear space around it: nothing overlaps a neighbour or a label. The same scale in every frame; the last frames lie on one floor line.

```text
THE GRAY KEEPING'S MATRIARCH-CLERIC -- a foe for a tactics game, drawn on five sheets. A female gnoll priestess of the hyena-god: bigger and heavier than a common gnoll, broad-shouldered and long-armed, a spotted hyena's head with a greying muzzle and a heavy grey ruff, scarred ears, pale knowing eyes. Over hide and mail she wears a long mantle of grey-brown hyena pelts and a collar of small bones and teeth; skull fetishes hang at her belt. She carries a tall staff of dark wood crowned with a hyena skull, and when she prays its eye-sockets burn with a pale green light. Old and powerful, not frail.

HEAD 1 -- THE MATRIARCH-CLERIC from the bottom-right: isometric three-quarter view from above, every frame facing toward the bottom-right corner of the image. Rows: Idle (6: standing tall, leaning on the skull-staff, the mantle stirring, head turning slowly); Walk (8: a heavy, deliberate stride toward the bottom-right, the staff swinging with her steps); Strike (6: she swings the skull-staff two-handed at a foe toward the bottom-right, then recovers); Pray (6: she raises the staff high in both hands, the skull's sockets flare pale green, a ring of green light pulses out at her feet, then she lowers it); Laugh (6: she throws back her head in a hyena's cackling laugh, shoulders shaking); Flinch (4: struck, she snarls and recoils, then steadies); Fall (6: she staggers, drops to her knees, and falls onto her side, the staff beside her; the last frame lies on the ground); Prone (2: knocked down but alive, pushing herself up on the staff).

HEAD 2 -- THE MATRIARCH-CLERIC from the top-right, seen from behind: isometric three-quarter view from above, every frame facing toward the top-right corner of the image, rows only. The same rows as HEAD 1, each drawn from behind facing the top-right: Idle (6); Walk (8); Strike (6); Pray (6); Laugh (6); Flinch (4); Fall (6); Prone (2).

HEAD 3 -- THE MATRIARCH-CLERIC straight from the front, facing the viewer: rows only, the same rows and counts as HEAD 1.

HEAD 4 -- THE MATRIARCH-CLERIC from the right side in profile, facing right: rows only, the same rows and counts as HEAD 1.

HEAD 5 -- THE MATRIARCH-CLERIC straight from behind, facing away from the viewer: rows only, the same rows and counts as HEAD 1.

Draw each HEAD above as its own separate image, in the order given: one sheet an image, never two sheets in one image. Every sheet: 16-bit pixel art animation sheet, SNES-era action RPG style, crisp dark outline, readable at small size. Isometric three-quarter view from above, the camera looking down at about thirty degrees, as in a tactics game. Flat dark navy background (a deep blue, not grey and not black). ONE sheet filling the whole image: no other panels, no title. Only the first sheet has a portrait and a turnaround -- top left one large portrait, beside it four stills labelled Front, Right, Back, Left; every later sheet is rows only and draws her exactly as the first sheet's turnaround shows her, the same look, colours and size. Labelled rows of frames, each row's name at its left, numbered 1 to N under each frame -- every number used once, none skipped, one drawing for each number. Every frame faces the way its HEAD says; a walk is animated in place, not travelling across the sheet. Every frame stands apart with clear space around it: nothing overlaps a neighbour or a label. The same scale in every row and on every sheet, feet on one baseline. No scenery except what a row names.
```
Cut as: a new sheet `gnollmatriarch_p1` (Idle -> idle, Walk -> walk, Strike -> attack, Pray -> cast, Laugh -> laugh, Flinch -> flinch, Fall -> hurt, Prone -> prone); HEAD 1 SE, HEAD 2 NE, HEAD 3 S, HEAD 4 E, HEAD 5 N, the cutter mirroring SE for SW, E for W, NE for NW. Medium, a head taller than a common gnoll. The Snoot's death-watch (`snoot-mode/js/data.js` `gkw` sheets) draws it once it is cut.

### The top-down places' tiles and props: Silverton, the Guano Mine's top levels, the Glowseep (asked 10-22 in art-wanted section 21; drawn 10-21/22 by the art desk, ART-111 to ART-113; CUT 10-22, `da7400c`, BUILT FROM THE LIST above)

Moved here whole 2026-10-22 by the top tiles seat, on his *"art 111-113 are in to see if we can give the top down something to work with"*. Every HEAD came back (paginated by the art desk's thirty-drawing ceiling: ART-111 twelve pages, ART-112 six, ART-113 four), with its known defects named in its CUTTER-NOTES. What was laid and what was not, and why, is the return note `deep16/_src/art-desk/sent/ENGINE-RETURN-2026-10-22-top-down-tiles.md`; for a re-roll, its OPEN list.


His words, 2026-10-22 (to the lanes desk): *"have the 2d places, silverton, surface guano mines and gallieries, the wet - compose a tile art request that includes variants and any props they want"*, then *"i meant glowseep, not wet"*. Read as every floor drawn top-down, north up, on the town's engine (`deep16/js/topview.js`): Silverton's streets and the rooms behind its doors (`deep16/js/town.js`); the Guano Mine's top levels -- the Crawler Warrens (`warrens_a` the mouth camp, `warrens_b` the stalls, `warrens_c` the workings) and the Guano Galleries (`galleries_g1` the mouth, `galleries_g2` the working gallery, `galleries_g3` the dens; `deep16/js/mines.js`); and the Glowseep (`M.SEEP_ROWS`). Every tile there is drawn by code today: one 48 px square a tile, four noise variants a kind, no edges or corners, one box for every crate, tent and sledge, one stone ring for every well, beam and fire pit, no flame, no stairs, no trees, no lamps. What he has said of the look: *"Silverton and the warrens prettier versions of what we had in the 8 bit"*; *"The roof brown and the road brown are too close together"*; *"Can we get some diagonal looking tiles to try and make the hex look better?"*; of the working gallery, *"giant brown blur, really"*; of the dens, *"too often hidden behind walls that should probably transluce"* (the see-through wall is the engine's job; the art gives the walls their faces). Section 17's shop props (HELD 10-21 *"till the town's tiles please him"*) are folded in here as the Silverton block's HEAD 7, on these words; section 17 stays as it was written. Sent to the art desk as `deep16/_src/art-desk/sent/ASK-2026-10-22-top-down-tiles.md` (carried 10-22, his *"outbox delivered"*).

```text
SILVERTON, TOP-DOWN (one image a HEAD):

SILVERTON -- a poor frontier mining town at the foot of a dwarven mountain, an early-Renaissance town of honest, worn things: timber-framed houses with pale plaster between dark beams, clay-tile, slate and shingle roofs, dusty streets, a dressed-stone plaza with a fountain, a river one tile wide, mine headframes over shafts at the town's edge, a six-sided timber fighting arena called the Hex. The roofs and the roads must never share a colour: the roads a pale dusty tan, the roofs red clay, blue-grey slate, cool grey shingle and pale stone. One tile is one step of a 16-bit RPG town map: a person stands about one tile tall, a house is two to four tiles across.

HEAD 1 -- THE GROUND: square ground tiles, four variants of each kind in a row, every variant tiling seamlessly with the others of its kind: Beaten earth (bare tan ground, a few pebbles) - Dirt road (paler dusty tan, faint wheel ruts: the streets) - Grass (sparse dry tufts on earth) - Dressed stone (square grey flagstones in staggered courses: the Gate Plaza and Fountain Street) - Threshold (a worn stone step-slab before a door) - Fountain water (clear blue, two frames of glints) - River water (deeper blue-green, moving, two frames) - Spoil (mine tailings: grey rubble scattered on earth). Then the edges, a full set for each (north, south, east, west, the four outer corners, the four inner corners): grass against earth; the dressed stone's kerb against the dirt road; the river's banks against earth. Then THE BANK: an earth bank one tile tall facing south, a stone lip along its top -- its left end, its middle, its right end -- and a stair of rough stone steps down it, two tiles wide.

HEAD 2 -- THE ROOFS: each roof as nine pieces that tile across a house of any size (north-west corner, north edge, north-east corner, west edge, middle, east edge, south-west corner, south edge, south-east corner; the ridge running east-west through the middle, the north slope in shadow, the south slope lit), and the same roof on a one-tile house: Red clay tile (the tall houses) - Blue-grey slate (the low houses and booths) - Cool grey shingle (the shacks: grey, not brown) - Pale stone (the tower) - and a wall-walk of grey blocks (the top of a compound's stone wall).

HEAD 3 -- THE WALLS, DOORS AND SIGNS: the south faces below the roofs, one tile wide each, two heights (a low house's two-thirds of a tile, a tall house's full tile), each with a left end, a middle and a right end: Timber-framed plaster (dark posts every half tile, a beam, pale plaster) - the same with a shuttered window - the same with a lit window (warm yellow) - Grey stone (the tower, the compound) - then the doors, each one tile wide in its wall: a store door standing open (a plank door ajar in a stone frame under a lintel) - a door shut and barred - a wide double door, iron-banded. Then the shop signs: a hanging plank sign on two chains from an iron bracket, blank, and the same sign with each of these painted on it, one each: a ring, a pair of scales, a coin, a potion bottle, a bed, a star, a pack, a candle, a sword, a needle and thread, a jar, a sun, a mortar and pestle.

HEAD 4 -- THE HEX AND THE MOUNTAIN: the Hex is a six-sided timber arena, so its pieces run on the diagonals: a log wall face for each of its six sides (two running east-west, four on the diagonals), the corners where two sides meet, its roof ring of pale stone over the stands in the same six directions, its south-tip double doors, and its floor of raked gold sand (four variants). The mountain at the town's north edge: its rock top (four variants, dark purple-grey stone, cracked), its cliff face one tile wide and a tile and a third tall (left end, middle, right end), and a vault door set into the cliff (iron bars over heavy planks).

HEAD 5 -- THE STREET'S PROPS, each drawn alone and labelled beside it: Market stall (a plank counter under a striped cloth awning, two tiles) - Crate - Barrel - Sacks - Handcart (two-wheeled) - Well (a stone ring with a winch and bucket) - Mine headframe (a timber tower over a shaft mouth, two by two tiles) - Lamp post (an iron post with a hooded lantern, lit) - Pine tree (gnarled, its crown over two by two tiles) - Bench - Hitching rail - Fountain (a round stone basin with a spout, two by two tiles) - Signpost - Notice board (a plank board on two posts, papers pinned to it).

HEAD 6 -- THE ROOMS' FLOORS AND WALLS (inside the shops, seen the same way): Plank floor, Flagstone floor, Earth floor (four variants each); the back wall seen from the south, a tile and a little tall: plaster between dark timbers above a skirting board (left end, middle, right end), the same with a window, the same with a stone fireplace, lit; an inside doorway with its door standing open.

HEAD 7 -- THE ROOMS' PROPS, each drawn alone and labelled beside it: Counter (a shop counter of dark varnished wood, waist high, its top worn pale, two tiles long, its front facing south) - Shelves (wall shelves to a man's head, packed with jars, folded cloth, small boxes and ledgers, their back against a north wall, two tiles long) - Grille (a moneychanger's counter with an iron grille above it, a slot at the bottom and a small brass pair of scales on top, two tiles long) - Beam scale (a weigh-house's great balance: a heavy timber beam on a stout post, two broad pans on chains, iron weights at its foot, two by two tiles) - Anvil (on a stump block) - Forge (a stone hearth with glowing coals, a leather bellows and a smoke hood, two tiles long) - Barrel - Sacks (grain sacks stacked three high) - Cloth rack (bolts of dyed cloth, red, blue and ochre) - Desk (a scrivener's slanted desk, an inkpot, a quill, an open ledger) - Pew (a plain wooden bench with a back, two tiles long) - Lantern rack (small brass lanterns, three lit) - Table (two tiles) - Chair - Barber's chair - Bath (a wooden tub, steaming) - Bed (a wooden frame bed with a blanket) - Stable stall (a plank partition with a manger).

ALDWIN -- the mission almoner. An aging priest, severe and watchful, in threadbare grey wool with a plain wooden token at the throat [seat]. Hands calloused from kneading bread, not from prayer. Quiet certainty in the face, and behind it the willingness to protect the guilty. Fifty years at the bread line at a frontier mission of the sun god's faith, far past its own writ: bread at six, at quarter past for the proud; the floor free, if the old man likes your face.

HEAD 4 -- SKEPTICAL (1, one drawing): weighing the face in front of him.
HEAD 5 -- CONCERNED (1, one drawing): a guarded refusal.
HEAD 6 -- WORK (6, two bands of three): takes up a round loaf from the counter, breaks it in two with his calloused hands, holds one half out toward the party (screen left), lays the other half down; the last frame the hands back at rest (anatomical right hand does the holding out; the left stays near the counter).

```text
THE HEX, INSIDE, TOP-DOWN (one image a HEAD):

THE HEX -- a six-sided timber fighting arena in a poor frontier mining town, seen from inside with the roof and upper floors cut away, as a 16-bit RPG shows a building's inside. A point of the six-sided shape faces due north and another due south, so four of its six walls run on the diagonals and the other two run straight north-south: every wall, rail, tier and edge piece below comes in those directions. On the ground floor a hexagon of raked gold sand sits in the middle, a board lip round it and two tiers of timber steps going up from it to a plank floor that runs out to the log walls, with four long bars, timber posts holding up the roof, and two spiral stairs by the north point. The second floor is the gambling floor: a ring of floor round a big opening over the sand, with a rail along the opening's edge, red rugs, green felt card tables, and cushioned benches for the slave owners on the south side. The third floor is the town council's meeting room under a big window in the north point, with an office and an armory either side of it. Honest worn timber, dark logs, brass and iron, lamplight. One tile is one step of a 16-bit RPG map: a person stands about one tile tall.

HEAD 1 -- THE FLOORS: square floor tiles, four variants of each kind in a row, every variant tiling seamlessly with the others of its kind: Plank floor (worn boards running east-west, the ground floor's concourse) - Upper tier (timber planks, a lighter step) - Lower tier (timber planks, a darker step) - Board lip (heavy boards at the sand's edge) - Dark polished boards (the council's floor) - Red rug (a deep red woven rug with a gold lattice) - Blue rug (the owners' lounge, the same weave in deep blue) - Doormat (a worn rush mat at a door). Then the edges, each a full set in the six directions (two running east-west, four on the diagonals) with the corners where two meet: the sand against the board lip; the lip stepping up to the lower tier; the lower tier stepping up to the upper tier; the upper tier stepping up to the plank floor -- on the north half each step shows its upright face (a lit timber riser), on the south half only its edge in shadow; the red rug's gold border against the plank floor; the blue rug's border.

HEAD 2 -- THE WALLS FROM INSIDE: the log wall seen from inside, on the two north diagonals: its inner face a tile and a third tall below a dark top, heavy logs laid in courses that follow the diagonal (left end, middle, right end); the same wall running straight north-south (its top only, a tile wide); the two south diagonals as a low stub wall (its top only, so the floor shows beyond it); the corners where two walls meet; the north point's double doors from inside (two plank leaves, the great log standing between them); the south point's open doorway from inside (two door posts); a single door in the straight east or west wall; THE BIG WINDOW: tall glass panes in heavy mullions set into the log wall on the two north diagonals, three tiles each side of the point; an inside timber wall on a diagonal (thin, a tile tall) with a plank door in it, and the same with a serving hatch shut behind two wooden shutters.

HEAD 3 -- THE GROUND FLOOR'S THINGS, each drawn alone and labelled beside it: The long bar on a diagonal (dark wood, its top worn pale, red plank front; an end, the middle, an end), and the same bar straight east-west; The bartender's back shelf (bottles, mugs, a keg tap); The Wall of Boxes (twenty-seven small iron strongboxes, nine across and three high, on a timber rack above the bartender's shelf, a few with names scratched off); An interior post (a round timber log post three feet thick, a wall's height); A spiral stair seen from above (wooden wedge steps winding round a central newel post, a rail round its edge, two tiles across); A guard station (a timber booth wall by a door, waist-high counter); The contraband box (a small iron-bound box with a padlock); A trestle table (plain boards, two benches); The odds slate (a large chalkboard on two legs, chalked columns of names and odds).

HEAD 4 -- THE UPPER FLOORS' THINGS, each drawn alone and labelled beside it: A felt card table (round, green baize, a wooden rim, cards and coin stacks on it) and a stool; The rail at the opening's edge (a timber handrail on turned balusters: straight east-west, on each diagonal, and curved); A cushioned bench (a long settle with deep red cushions); An empty fine chair (high-backed, red velvet); The council's long table (dark polished wood, four tiles long) and a council chair; A heavy desk with papers and an inkwell; An iron strongbox; A weapon rack (spears, axes and round shields); An armory chest (iron-banded); A hanging lantern on a wall hook, lit.

HEAD 5 -- THE HEX FROM OUTSIDE, STRAIGHT DOWN (the town map's view, as the town's houses are drawn: from directly above and a little to the south, NOT isometric, NOT angled): the Hex is a six-sided arena with a point due north and a point due south, so its outline has two straight north-south sides (east and west) and four diagonal sides. Its roof is a ring of pale stone open to the sky in the middle: the ring drawn as flat bands following each of the six sides (stone courses running along the side), the hips where two bands meet, the inner edge round the opening. Under the two south diagonal sides, the log walls' south faces show below the roof edge, the logs laid along the slant; the east and west sides show no face, only the roof's edge. At the south point the wall is cut flat for a pair of iron-banded double doors facing straight south, under the roof's point. Pieces: each roof band (north-west, north-east, east, west, south-west, south-east diagonals and straight runs), the six corners where bands meet, the inner opening's edge on each side, the log wall face on each south diagonal (left end, middle, right end), the south doors closed, and the same doors open.

Draw each HEAD above as its own separate image, in the order given: one sheet an image, never two sheets in one image. Every sheet: 16-bit pixel art tiles and props, SNES-era top-down RPG (A Link to the Past's look), crisp dark outline where a thing stands up, readable at small size. Seen from above and a little to the south, north up: the top of a thing from above and its south face below it; light from the upper left. Every tile square and the same size, 48 by 48 pixels, on an even grid with a 1-pixel gap, each labelled beside it, the variants of a kind side by side in a row. Props each alone with clear space around it, all at one scale: a thing on one tile fills it, a thing on two lies across two side by side. Flat dark navy background (a deep blue, not grey and not black). ONE sheet filling the whole image: no other panels, no title; nothing overlaps a neighbour or a label. No characters, and no labels on the tiles or props themselves.
```
Cut as: tiles by a `tools/hexin-sheet.py` into `hexin_p1`; `deep16/js/hex.js` paints HEAD 1 under its floors in place of HX.ground / HX.gambling / HX.third's code (the four variants by the square, the edges by each square's place on the tiers' rings -- its face of six and its band), and stands HEAD 2's walls (HX.pieces: the shell's faces by direction, the carved north doors, the Big Window, the inner walls and the shuttered hatches), HEAD 3's and HEAD 4's things in place of its code-drawn blocks (the four bars, the Wall of Boxes, the posts, the spirals, the guard stations and box, the boards, the slate; the felt tables and stools, the rail's runs and bow, the owners' benches, Vair's chair, the council's table and chairs, the desk, strongbox, racks and chest). HEAD 5 stands in topview.js's hexCanvas (the Hex on the town floor) for the code's roof ring, walls and tip doors. The sand is ART-111's (`hex_sand` in `toptiles_p1`, as js/topview.js TV.piecePx reads it for the Hex's outside). The Hex's people keep their stand-in figures (a figure is a five-HEAD block of its own, not tiles).

### The lamia's human form (asked 10-28 in art-wanted section 24; drawn 10-28 by the art desk, ART-120, PARTIAL; CUT 10-28, `d5372a1d`, BUILT FROM THE LIST above)

Moved here whole 2026-10-28 by the first cutter seat (started by the lanes desk; his *"check fresh - one cutter at a time should be fine"*). Every HEAD came back; the walks are open by the art desk's own notes. The block as it was asked:

His words, his ear file of 10-28 (0156Z/0215Z), on the gallery's creatures shelf at the lamia: *"needs human form idle, perhaps others - add art request"*. Since `8f815a3` (the first cutter, the bestiary lane's §37, its lean 1) the lamia stands disguised at the start of a fight -- Disguise Self, the robed woman the art desk drew as frame 6 of her Disguise row -- till her first turn or a wound; on the grid that woman is one still frame (`lamia_p1` row `still`), and she reveals by the Disguise row played backwards (`reveal`). This asks her human form its own rows, five views as RULED 10-14: an Idle to stand in, and a Walk and a Cast for when she keeps the disguise while she moves or casts (Disguise Self lasts an hour and casting does not end it; whether she keeps it past her first turn is his word, below). Her Cast is the gesture alone: since 10-28 the code draws her spell's light at her hand (js/looks.js LK.spark, his *"have code draw it when she casts"*), so the art draws none.

### The lamia's human form
ATTACH `deep16/_src/lamia/ART-20/ART-20_HEAD-1_PAGE-1.png` (her portrait and turnaround: the face, the hair, the gold) and her five Disguise pages -- `ART-20_HEAD-1_PAGE-8.png` (from the bottom-right), `ART-20_HEAD-2_PAGE-7.png` (top-right), `ART-20_HEAD-3_PAGE-7.png` (front), `ART-20_HEAD-4_PAGE-7.png` (right side), `ART-20_HEAD-5_PAGE-7.png` (behind): frame 6 of each is the woman, as she must look in that view.
```text
Attached: a foe from the same game, the lamia, and the five sheets of her Disguise -- frame 6 of each is the ordinary woman she disguises herself as, seen from that sheet's side. Draw that woman: the same face, hair and size as frame 6 shows her, in the same pixel style.

THE LAMIA IN HER HUMAN FORM -- a foe in disguise for a tactics game, drawn on five sheets. An ordinary-looking desert woman standing on two legs: long, wavy black hair falling past her shoulders, dark-lined eyes, a fine gold circlet with one teal stone on her brow, small gold earrings; a plain, loose, hooded robe of sand-coloured cloth with long wide sleeves, gathered at the waist by a broad brown sash, falling to her ankles; simple leather sandals. No dagger, no jewelled collar, no lion's body: nothing about her shows what she is. Calm and watchful, a little too graceful.

HEAD 1 -- THE WOMAN from the bottom-right: isometric three-quarter view from above, every frame facing toward the bottom-right corner of the image. Rows: Idle (6: standing at ease, one hand resting at the front of her robe, a slow breath, the robe's hem and her hair stirring a little; frame 6 matches frame 1); Walk (8: an unhurried, graceful walk toward the bottom-right, the robe swinging; animate in place, not travelling across the sheet); Cast (6: she raises one hand and spreads her fingers toward the bottom-right as if weaving something in the air, holds it, then lowers it; draw NO light, glow, sparkle or magic of any kind -- the game draws the spell itself).

HEAD 2 -- THE WOMAN from the top-right, seen from behind: isometric three-quarter view from above, every frame facing toward the top-right corner of the image, rows only. The same rows as HEAD 1, each drawn from behind facing the top-right: Idle (6); Walk (8); Cast (6, no light).

HEAD 3 -- THE WOMAN straight from the front, facing the viewer: rows only, the same rows and counts as HEAD 1.

HEAD 4 -- THE WOMAN from the right side in profile, facing right: rows only, the same rows and counts as HEAD 1.

HEAD 5 -- THE WOMAN straight from behind, facing away from the viewer: rows only, the same rows and counts as HEAD 1.

Draw each HEAD above as its own separate image, in the order given: one sheet an image, never two sheets in one image. Every sheet: 16-bit pixel art animation sheet, SNES-era action RPG style, crisp dark outline, readable at small size. Isometric three-quarter view from above, the camera looking down at about thirty degrees, as in a tactics game. Flat dark navy background (a deep blue, not grey and not black). ONE sheet filling the whole image: no other panels, no title. Only the first sheet has a portrait and a turnaround -- top left one large portrait, beside it four stills labelled Front, Right, Back, Left; every later sheet is rows only and draws her exactly as the first sheet's turnaround shows her, the same look, colours and size. Labelled rows of frames, each row's name at its left, numbered 1 to N under each frame -- every number used once, none skipped, one drawing for each number. Every frame faces the way its HEAD says; a walk is animated in place, not travelling across the sheet. Every frame stands apart with clear space around it: nothing overlaps a neighbour or a label. The same scale in every row and on every sheet, feet on one baseline. No scenery except what a row names.
```
Cut as: rows onto `lamia_p1` (tools/lamia-sheet.py) -- Idle -> `still` (the woman she stands as, a breath now where it is one frame), Walk -> `stillwalk`, Cast -> `stillcast` (her spark drawn by the code, tools/castspark.py); HEAD 1 SE, HEAD 2 NE, HEAD 3 S, HEAD 4 E, HEAD 5 N, the cutter mirroring SE for SW, E for W, NE for NW. Each view scaled by the Disguise row's frame 6 of the same view (the woman already on the grid), so she is the same size she reveals from. **Walk and Cast play only on his word:** today she drops the disguise on her first turn (the first cutter's lean 1); kept while she walks and casts and dropped at her first blow or a wound, they would play.

### The generic man and the generic woman (asked 10-28 in art-wanted section 25; drawn 10-28 by the art desk, ART-122; CUT 10-28, `a22dd2e4`, BUILT FROM THE LIST above)

Moved here whole 2026-10-28 by the fourth cutter seat (started by the lanes desk; his *"generic NPCs a  have landed in fresh"*). Every page came back, the woman's last two in a supplement; the art desk's own notes leave the likeness and the fine props for his look. The block as it was asked:


His words, his ear files of 10-28 (relayed by the lanes desk): *"art request for a generic NPC face portrait with 'drinker, gambler, and any other variants we need (guano scraper, etc.) where we do variants instead of 'skeptical' and similar we have for the good NPCs ..."*; and on the first draft's eighteen strangers (relayed ~04:10Z): *"Yes and I want to lean into it. Like "Generic NPC (maybe male and female)" as a specific person with each function as a costume/look they have"*. So two people, each one identity -- the same face, hair and build on every page -- dressed for each job the crowds need: the costumes where the named have their moods (ATTENTIVE, WELCOMING, SKEPTICAL, CONCERNED). They are the man and the woman of the art desk's townsfolk (ART-09 SE and NE, ART-52 S, E and N; cut 10-27 as `folkman_p1` and `folkwoman_p1`, the commoners who flee the Skylights) [seat: the faces then belong to bodies the game already draws]. Today the unnamed of Silverton's street, the Hex, the Crawler Warrens, the Guano Galleries and the Glowseep (content/npcs.json, content/maps/*.json `npcs`, deep16/js/mines.js) speak on a plain card and stand on the floors as the foes' crewman, brawler, bandit and guard (deep16/js/town.js T.KIND); with these, on the counter screen as the named do (deep16/js/counter.js), each in the costume of the job they stand at. The street's boy and girl (`towns4`, `towns8`) are not in it and keep their card [seat].

### The generic man
ATTACH `deep16/_src/townsfolk/ART-52/ART-52_HEAD-3_PAGE-1.png` (the townsfolk from the front: its Man rows are the man) and `deep16/_src/townsfolk/ART-09_HEAD-1_PAGE-1.png` (the same two from the bottom-right), and `deep16/_src/winters/ART-78/ART-78_HEAD-1_PAGE-1.png` and `ART-78_HEAD-1_PAGE-6.png` (the portrait pages' shape, for the format only, not the face).
```text
THE GENERIC MAN -- one ordinary man of a frontier mining town, and the same man on every page: the man of the attached townsfolk sheets -- shaggy brown hair, a full brown beard, a weathered, good-natured face, about forty [seat], a working man's build. On HEAD 1 in the man's own clothes as the sheets show them: a cream shirt with the sleeves rolled, a brown leather apron, blue trousers, brown boots. On every later HEAD dressed for a different job: a costume over the same face, hair and build, the hair and beard combed or tied back as a job wants, never changed; only the clothes and what is in the hands change. Nobody heroic, nobody grotesque.

HEAD 1 -- IDLE (6, two bands of three): in the man's own clothes, a breathing and blink loop at the counter, hands resting on it; loops cleanly.
HEAD 2 -- THE DRINKER (1): a stained work shirt open at the collar, sallow and stubbled, a clay mug of ale held on the ledge, eyes a little too bright.
HEAD 3 -- THE GAMBLER (1): a good coat gone shiny at the cuffs over a waistcoat, rings on two fingers, a fan of cards and a short stack of coins on the ledge, a measuring look.
HEAD 4 -- THE BARKEEP (1): sleeves rolled, a leather barman's apron, a rag over one shoulder, wiping a mug.
HEAD 5 -- THE HIRED HAND (1): a day laborer of the hiring corner: a sweat-stained shirt, a coil of rope over one shoulder.
HEAD 6 -- THE SHAFT HAND (1): a miner off shift: a dusty leather jerkin, a candle-stub helmet pushed back, grime in the creases of the face and knuckles.
HEAD 7 -- THE GUANO SCRAPER (1): a scraper of the Guano Galleries: a cloth tied over nose and mouth pulled down to speak, a hooded lamp, a long-handled scraper, everything powdered pale grey-brown with guano dust.
HEAD 8 -- THE CREW BOSS (1): a tally stick and a hooded lamp, a whistle on a cord, the look of someone counting heads.
HEAD 9 -- THE DRIVE SPEAR (1): a bat-drive hand of the Galleries: a short spear held upright, a leather cap and shoulder guard, watching the dark above.
HEAD 10 -- THE CRAWLER HAND (1): a hand of the Crawler Warrens' pens: leather gloves to the elbow, a milking thimble on a thong at the throat, wary and patient.
HEAD 11 -- THE GUARD (1): a hired guard: a padded jack and an iron cap, a spear haft at the shoulder, bored and watchful.
HEAD 12 -- THE CLERK (1): a warehouse clerk: sleeve-guards and a plain waistcoat, a pen behind the ear, a wax tablet on the ledge.

Waist-up behind a plain dark wooden counter ledge, a stable eye-level three-quarter front camera, looking screen left at someone just beside the camera; the head and body the same size on every page as on the Idle page. Each image 1440 x 810, ONE action an image, six-frame actions in two bands of three with clear gutters; the counter ledge under the hands on every frame, its top edge at the same height. ### The one-handed slash, skinned over a mannequin: Barley in mail, five views (asked 10-31 in art-wanted section 34; drawn 11-04 by the art desk, BARLEY-SLASH-PILOT-2026-11-04, N held; CUT 11-04, `5c53084d`)


Griz, 10-31: *"What if we did stick figure modeling in blender for the various attacks (1H slashing (longswordish), 1H piercing (rapierish), and gave the image gens a stick-figure request with character art 'skin these figures with this character'"*. One family first, to see whether the generator follows a pose reference before the rest are built. Blender pins the motion, the timing, the five views, the size and the feet (`tools/mannequin-blend.py`, then `tools/mannequin-sheet.py`: the strips, the grid and the rig's numbers in `deep16/art-src/mannequin/`, and how to judge what comes back in its README); the generator only skins it. The hero is Barley in mail (`barley_p3`, ART-109): drawn empty-handed, his weapon drawn by the engine in his fists, and no one-handed blow of his own -- a longsword plays the flail sweep today (`deep16-hero-poses.md`). The ask was first the 10-30 way (*"code-drawn weapon variability with strike pose by weapon type"*: the fist empty, the engine drawing the blade), and free Grok, asked that way, drew a punch, not a cut (the score in `deep16/art-src/mannequin/README.md`). **RULED 10-31**, Griz: *"we can put this on hold til GPT available wed. We'll send the mannequin with the sword along with asking the draw to include it"* -- the blocks below ask for the sword drawn in his hand along the bar. Five blocks, one an image, in the order RULED 10-14 (SE, NE, S, E, N); attach to each the identity page and that view's strip.

```text
ATTACH two images: 1) ART-109-IDENTITY.png -- the hero BARLEY in his chainmail hauberk and boots, Front, Right, Back, Left: draw exactly this young man, his spiky straw-gold hair, the grey chainmail hauberk to the knees with its belt, the dark sleeves and trousers, the brown boots, his build and proportions; 2) slash-SE.png -- a REFERENCE STRIP: a plain jointed mannequin doing the move, six numbered frames. Skin this figure with this character: draw Barley in each frame in exactly the mannequin's pose, frame for frame.

How to read the mannequin: BLUE limbs are his RIGHT arm and leg, ORANGE his LEFT; grey is his body; the nose on the pale head shows which way his face turns. The magenta bar in his blue (right) hand is his sword: draw a plain steel longsword in his RIGHT hand exactly along the bar -- the grip in his closed fist at the gold ring, a simple crossguard there, the straight blade lying along the magenta bar out to its pale tip, the same length in every frame. His left hand is an empty fist.

HEAD 1 -- BARLEY - SLASH SE (6): a one-handed sword cut, from high on his right down across to low on his left, seen from the bottom-right, every frame facing toward the bottom-right corner of the image. Both boots stay planted the whole time, the left foot forward. 1 the guard, the right fist low in front of him; 2 the wind-up, the right fist raised beside his head, his body turned to his right, the left fist forward; 3 the swing coming over, the right fist above his right shoulder; 4 THE HIT: the right arm reaching out at the foe, the body turned into the blow, the left fist back at the hip; 5 the follow-through, the right fist low on his left; 6 back to the guard.

Draw this as ONE image, like the art desk's ART-109 pages: 16-bit pixel art animation sheet, SNES-era action RPG style, crisp dark outline, readable at small size. Isometric three-quarter view from above, the camera looking down at about thirty degrees, the same camera as the strip. Flat dark navy background (a deep blue, not grey and not black). The title BARLEY - SLASH SE at the top; six frames in one row, numbered 1 to 6 under each frame, every number used once. Each frame copies the strip's frame of the same number: the same pose, the same turn of the body, his fists where the mannequin's hands are, the sword along the bar, the same size in every frame; his boots exactly where the mannequin's feet are, on one baseline in every frame -- his feet never move in this move. Every frame stands apart with clear space around it. No scenery, no shield, no motion lines, none of the mannequin's colours on Barley.
```

### 36. The Halfway Inn's props and walls, for the diamonds (added 11-04, the Inn build seat) -- READY, in the outbox (`deep16/_src/outbox/ASK-2026-11-04-halfway-inn-props.md`), for the art desk's next budget

Griz, 11-04, on the inn's eyes row (his ear file 0506Z), verbatim: *"There should be a big fire in the center, with the common room on the road side of it and the kitchen on the other. There should be a long table across one wall and a bench by the fire, and a table with two seats - as well as the bar counter underneath the stairs. Two bedrooms with a small fireplace on the other end of the kitchen (a one-story part of the building) - barn big enough to house 6 horses / Prop request list for the art-department, wall tilings as needed as well"*. The floor is laid to it (`deep16/js/inn.js`, `deep16/?innshow`); every prop stands as the code's stand-in till these come back. Eight pages, the paste in the outbox file: the big fire (two-faced, lit) and the small fireplace; the common room's long table, the bench by the fire, the table for two and its chairs, the bar counter under the stair; the kitchen's tub, worktable, the shelf of hung fish; the rooms' bed, bedside table, chest; the barn's horse stall (six, either side of an aisle), its door, hay; the yard's well, hitching rail, woodpile, Amara's wagon, the rowboat, the lantern post, the flat stone; the inn's fieldstone walls in two stories and the wing's one, the barn's planks, the cut stub for inside; the red tile roofs and the barn's shingle. Where: the inn's floor on the diamonds (one square a figure's footing). Cut as: a cutter's `tools/innprops-sheet.py` over `tools/sheetrows.py`, the pieces into the diamonds' props (the code's stand-ins today: js/iso.js blocks, the chimney a rock column) -- the first art-desk props on an iso floor, so the cutter wires the drawing too.

**Added 11-04 by the lanes desk** (Griz at the pane on the inn, verbatim: *"as a key location, we'll probably art request tiles and props for it, see with what we're already requesting in that vein and add to it"*; and his *"move the stairs to ascend from 20, 23 toward 25, 23 (such that headroom behind the bar is nearer the fire)"*): PAGE 2's stair re-drawn to the floor as it stands now -- six squares along the south wall behind the bar, its foot at the west end rising east toward the big fire, the barman's headroom under its high end; and a PAGE 9 -- the long table laid for supper (THE MEAL's picture, an overlay for the table) and the table for two laid; the stair's head and the chimney through the upper floor; the two-story faces with their windows lit for the night, and the lamp over each door lit and unlit; the inn sign on its post by the road; the kitchen's kettle, hearth tools and bench; the room doors inside as frames at the stub's height; the lake's shallows as a tile and the night-lines' floats, bobbing and still; the trough by the rail and the wagon's ruts round the yard. The outbox file carries both; nine pages now.

### Ambrose Winters' poses for the ring and the copper scraping (asked 10-21 in art-wanted section 19; drawn 10-30 by the art desk, ART-78-SCENES-2026-10-30-I: present, nod, averted, drawer; CUT 11-04, `a4699972 to 0e635549`, onto `pt_winters`)


His words, 2026-10-21 (to the lanes desk, of the Ring of Binding and the copper scraping): *"they'll be in this one too, do you need more poses?"*. Yes: his six ART-78 pages (idle, four dialogue stills, the acquisition) cover his errands and his shelves (`deep16/js/counter.js`, the counter's screen); these are the moments his two held scenes and his own words name that no page draws. HEADs 1-4 are wanted; HEADs 5-6 are optional (his ledger and pen, which his words describe and no page shows). Drawn as ART-78 was, so `tools/portrait-sheet.py` cuts them as it cut his six. Sent to the art desk as `deep16/_src/art-desk/sent/ASK-2026-10-21-winters-poses.md`.

```text
AMBROSE WINTERS, MORE POSES (one image a HEAD). ATTACH deep16/_src/winters/ART-78/ART-78_HEAD-1_PAGE-1.png (his identity: the Idle page) and ART-78_HEAD-1_PAGE-6.png (his hands on the counter: the Acquisition page). The same man, the same clothes, the same camera, scale and counter as those pages: do not redesign him.

AMBROSE WINTERS -- dealer in acquisitions and estates. A human man whose face does not agree with itself: the eyes and mouth of a man in his fifties set in skin that has gone suddenly, unevenly old -- deep crepe at the throat and temples, a young man's jaw beneath it, hair white at one temple and dark at the other. Excellent old clothes, decades out of date and immaculately kept: an oxblood doublet with small round buttons, a slate-grey coat, a bone-white collar and cuffs. Waist-up behind a plain dark wooden counter ledge, three-quarter front, looking screen left at someone just beside the camera.

HEAD 1 -- PRESENT (6, two bands of three): the Ring of Binding. 1 his hands resting on the counter, looking at the party; 2 his right hand (screen left) goes into his waistcoat; 3 it brings out a plain ring of dull metal between finger and thumb, held up a moment; 4 he sets it on the counter in front of him; 5 two fingers slide it a hand's width toward the party (screen left); 6 his hand lifted away, both hands resting again either side, the ring on the counter. The ring small but clear on every frame it is in.

HEAD 2 -- NOD (3, one band of three): "This time he nods." 1 the assessing look of his Skeptical page, chin a touch raised; 2 a slow single nod, chin down, eyes still on the party; 3 the head back up, the look eased, a guarded approval -- not a smile.

HEAD 3 -- AVERTED (1, one drawing): "Winters glances at what's in your hand, and then, carefully, doesn't." His eyes turned deliberately down and away from the party's hands, toward the counter's far end (screen right); the face composed and careful; hands still on the counter.

HEAD 4 -- DRAWER (6, two bands of three): a small curl of copper scraping put away. 1 his hands on the counter, a small curl of dull copper scraping lying in front of him, his eyes not on it; 2 he takes it up between finger and thumb without looking at it; 3 his hand goes down below the counter's edge, out of sight, his shoulder dipping; 4 the hand comes back up empty but for a small iron key; 5 he turns the key once at the counter's front edge, a short firm turn, eyes on the party; 6 the key gone into his waistcoat, both hands resting on the counter. Nothing written, nothing said: for him "a kind of shouting".

HEAD 5 (optional) -- WRITE (6, two bands of three): his ledger. 1 a ledger open on the counter, his right hand writing a line with a dip pen, his eyes on the page; 2-3 the pen moving along the line; 4 the line finished, the pen still on the page; 5 he looks up from the ledger at the party; 6 the pen lifted a little off the page, held there: "Winters waits, pen lifted."

HEAD 6 (optional) -- PEN DOWN (1, one drawing): "For once he sets the pen down." The ledger open on the counter, the pen laid flat across it, both his hands resting on the counter, looking straight at the party, attentive.

16-bit pixel-art cut-scene portrait animation, comparable to his ART-78 pages and to Sylvia Swann's. Waist-up, the stable eye-level three-quarter front camera of ART-78, his head and body the same size on every page as on its Idle page; crisp pixel clusters and restrained shading. Flat dark navy background (a deep blue, not grey and not black). Each image 1440 x 810, ONE action an image, the frames in bands of three with clear gutters between them; the counter ledge under his hands on every frame, as on the Acquisition page, its top edge at the same height on every frame. A title and frame numbers as on ART-78's pages, kept well clear of the drawings: a clear gap of navy between the title and the top of his hair, and between each number and the drawing. Nothing overlaps a neighbour. No scenery, no shop interior, no UI or border.
```
Cut as: `tools/portrait-sheet.py`, one line for his supplement in `PEOPLE` (its folder `deep16/_src/winters/<id>/` and a layout: HEAD 1 PRESENT 6 as two bands, HEAD 2 NOD 3 as one band, HEAD 3 AVERTED 1, HEAD 4 DRAWER 6 as two bands, HEADs 5-6 if drawn) into rows `present`, `nod`, `averted`, `drawer` (`write`, `pendown`) on `pt_winters`; the counter is cut off at its top as on his six pages. `deep16/js/counter.js` plays them in the ring's scene (winters.ready, winters.ring), the scraping's (deep.wintersCurl, deep.wintersPaid), and his menu's "pen lifted" -- when those scenes come to the grid with the lake.

Attached: two portrait pages from the same game, for the format only; a reference for a figure's size; a sheet of a caster from the same game, for the frame size and the shape of a Cast row; and the game's present Willem, for his colours and build.

WILLEM GLASS -- a human man of about thirty-five, slim and fair-haired, a former town factor gone to the road: a good navy coat worn shabby at the cuffs, a factor's white collar gone grey, long clever hands, a face made for being liked; no staff and no wand -- the hands are the instrument [seat: the look; the navy and the fair hair the game's; the factor the register's].

HEAD 1 -- IDLE (6, two bands of three): a breathing and blink loop at the table, a coin walking across the knuckles of one hand; loops cleanly.
HEAD 2 -- ATTENTIVE (1): neutral listening.
HEAD 3 -- WELCOMING (1): easy charm.
HEAD 4 -- SKEPTICAL (1): weighing the face in front of him.
HEAD 5 -- CONCERNED (1): a romantic's alarm.
HEAD 6 -- WORK (6, two bands of three): the coin walks across his knuckles, he closes his hand, opens it empty, and produces the coin from behind his other ear -- a trick, not a spell: draw no light; the last frame the hands back at rest.

PYRONIMUS “PYRO” SILVERSANDS, King of Sólskaft. A dwarf, ancient even by dwarven count: a soldier of the Orc War eighty years gone, who fought it beside men long since dead of old age, and has stood guard at the same vault door for the seventy years since. Short and enormously broad through the shoulders and neck, built like the door he keeps, and not stooped by any of it. Long full white beard and white hair. A deeply lined, weathered face with old battle scars gone pale, heavy brows, deep-set steady pale eyes that have watched friends age and die. A plain gold crown with short points, worn low, like something put on after the soldier was already finished. Heavy dwarven plate in dark blue-grey steel, superbly kept but visibly old, with a king’s grey mantle over the shoulders. A short-hafted hand mace at each hip, the off-hand one burning white when drawn. Grave, patient and warm under it: he likes adventurers because he was one. Seventy years of standing in one place is in his face, and none of it is boredom.

### Ásdís Scalebeam, the old kinswoman over the west store -- a talking portrait and a town figure in all five views
ATTACH `pt_ingrith.png` and `ingrith_p1.png` (the game's own Ingrith, her younger kinswoman: the FAMILY's look and colouring -- draw an old woman of the same blood, not the same face), `folkdwarf_p1.png` (a dwarf town figure from the same game: the build, the walking style and the camera), `ART-78_HEAD-1_PAGE-1.png` and `ART-78_HEAD-1_PAGE-6.png` (the portrait pages' shape, for the format only, not the face) and `REF-2026-10-21-town-figure-size.png` (a grown human figure's size, for scale: a dwarf stands about three quarters of it and broader).
```text
Attached: the portrait and walking figure of a dwarf woman from the same game -- a younger kinswoman of the dwarf asked for here; draw an OLD woman of the same family, the same colouring gone grey, not the same face. A dwarf town figure from the same game, for a dwarf's build, the walking style and the camera. Two portrait pages from the same game, for the format only. A size reference for scale.

ÁSDÍS SCALEBEAM -- an OLD DWARF WOMAN, the last of her family still living in a mountain hold that everyone else left. Forty families went back down into the deep and she would not go: she keeps one lamp lit on an empty street, bakes bread because nobody else will, and feeds any guest who looks like they eat standing up. Short and broad as a dwarf is, but an old woman's breadth, not a soldier's. The family's colouring from the attached kinswoman, gone grey [seat: her hair grey-white, braided and pinned up out of the way of the hearth]. A lined, plain, capable face: a cook and a mender, not a warrior and not a priest. Steady eyes that miss little and a mouth that says less than she knows. Plain house clothes [seat: a wool dress in a dull colour, a much-washed apron, sleeves rolled to the elbow, a shawl over the shoulders]; flour or thread on her hands, never a weapon. Warm, dry, and immovable: she is kind in the way of someone who has decided to be, and she has not once been talked out of anything.

HEAD 1 -- IDLE (6, two bands of three): a breathing and blink loop, standing with her hands folded in her apron; loops cleanly.
HEAD 2 -- ATTENTIVE (1): listening, head a little to one side, a ladle or a piece of mending stilled in her hands.
HEAD 3 -- WELCOMING (1): a small real smile, one hand out toward a seat at her table.
HEAD 4 -- REMEMBERING (1): fond, eyes off to one side at something long ago, the smile nearly there.
HEAD 5 -- GRAVE (1): the warmth put away, eyes level, hands still: an old decision she stands by and takes no pleasure in.
HEAD 6 -- FIRM (1): chin up, one brow raised, pointing at a bowl: an order to eat.

HEAD 7 -- THE TOWN FIGURE from the front, facing the viewer (south). Rows: Idle (4: standing with her hands folded in her apron, a small breath); Walk (8: a short, unhurried, sure walk toward the viewer, the shawl and apron moving; animate in place, not travelling across the sheet).
HEAD 8 -- THE TOWN FIGURE from the bottom-right, every frame facing toward the bottom-right corner of the image. Rows: Idle (4) and Walk (8), as HEAD 7.
HEAD 9 -- THE TOWN FIGURE from the right side in profile, facing right. Rows: Idle (4) and Walk (8), as HEAD 7.
HEAD 10 -- THE TOWN FIGURE from the top-right, seen from behind, every frame facing toward the top-right corner of the image. Rows: Idle (4) and Walk (8), as HEAD 7.
HEAD 11 -- THE TOWN FIGURE straight from behind, facing away from the viewer. Rows: Idle (4) and Walk (8), as HEAD 7.

HEADs 1-6 (the talking portrait): 16-bit pixel-art cut-scene portrait animation, comparable to the attached portrait pages. Waist-up, NO counter: she stands in the open, cut off at the waist by the bottom of the frame, a stable three-quarter front camera at HER eye level (a dwarf: do not draw her looked down on), looking screen left at someone just beside the camera; the head and body the same size on every page as on the Idle page. Crisp pixel clusters and restrained shading. Flat dark navy background (a deep blue, not grey and not black). Each image 1440 x 810, ONE action an image, the six-frame action in two bands of three with clear gutters. A title and frame numbers kept well clear of the drawings. No scenery, no UI or border.

HEADs 7-11 (the town figure): 16-bit pixel art animation sheet, SNES-era action RPG style, crisp dark outline, readable at small size. Isometric three-quarter view from above, the camera looking down at about thirty degrees, as in a tactics game -- the grid's own figures. The whole figure head to foot, a DWARF's proportions: about three quarters the height of a grown human and broader, as the attached dwarf town figure (a grown human stands about 50 pixels from sole to crown at game size; draw it large, the cutter brings it down). Flat dark navy background (a deep blue, not grey and not black). ONE sheet filling the whole image: no portrait, no other panels, no title. Labelled rows of frames, each row's name at its left, numbered 1 to N under each frame -- every number used once, none skipped. Every frame faces the way its HEAD says; the walk is animated in place, not travelling across the sheet. Every frame stands apart with clear space around it. The same scale in every row, feet on one baseline. No scenery.
```

His words earlier the same day: *"note I think we have text that says talmok fights with an axe on the road not his fists"*. Confirmed by the lanes desk: `content/text.json` `hex.intro.talmok` says "His greataxe is road iron; it never comes into the pit. Pit fists only."; his cut sheet `talmok_p2` has no axe in any row -- its attack is the Pit Fists, and its idle and walk show empty hands (looked at 11-19). So four rows are asked, in this order: Greataxe 6 (the blow on frame 4), Axe Idle 4, Axe Walk 8, Axe Flinch 4; one page a view and a row, `ART-WANTED-84-TALMOK-GREATAXE_HEAD-<1..5>_PAGE-<1..4>.png`. RULED 2026-11-19, Griz: *"1 - one blade is right, 2 - keep the flinch"* -- the axe has one blade, and Axe Flinch stays in the ask.

The guide: a human mannequin as tall as his own idle (56 rows), both hands on one haft the same distance apart in every frame, the right the upper hand -- 1 the guard at port, 2 the lift up his right side, 3 the top (the hands over his brow, the left foot coming off the floor), 4 THE CHOP (the foot stepped in, the blade down in front at chest height), 5 through to knee height, 6 back toward the guard. Strips and positions: `deep16/art-src/greataxe/` (`tools/twinmace-blend.py -- build kit=greataxe`, `tools/twinmace-sheet.py greataxe`, ``8930b3c5``).

PAGE 2 -- Axe Idle (4): standing in the guard of the Greataxe row's frame 1, the axe at port across his chest in both hands, a slow breath, a blink on 3.
PAGE 3 -- Axe Walk (8, two bands of four): a heavy, easy walk, the axe carried at port across his chest in both hands, its head by his right shoulder; two alternating half-strides -- one foot's contact, passing, the OTHER foot's contact, passing -- knees bending; animate in place, not travelling across the sheet.
PAGE 4 -- Axe Flinch (4): struck, he rocks back a half step with the axe pulled in across his body in both hands, shakes it off, comes forward into the guard again.

HEAD 1 -- from the front, facing the viewer (south). HEAD 2 -- from the bottom-right, every frame facing toward the bottom-right corner of the image. The whole figure head to foot AND the whole axe inside the frame, the same size and proportions as on his attached pages (he stands about 57 pixels from sole to crown at game size -- exactly the mannequin's height; draw it large, the cutter brings it down). Flat dark navy background (a deep blue, not grey and not black). ONE row of frames an image, its name at its left, numbered 1 to N under each frame -- every number used once, none skipped, one drawing for each number. Every frame stands apart with clear space around it, the raised axe included: nothing overlaps a neighbour or a label. The same scale in every frame, page and view; feet on one baseline. No scenery, no ground, no second figure, no rage, glow, blood or impact: the game draws those.
